correctness.rationale: The Fermat prime has group order 2^16. Thirteen explicitly listed modular 16384-th powers are plus/minus 256, whose squares are -1; hence all thirteen residues have exact order 65536. For every odd extension degree the multiplicative order stays 65536 (so nonprimitive) while Euler nonsquare exponent is multiplied by an odd repunit (so nonsquare). For odd prime degree ell every odd prime factor r of the repunit has ord_r(65537)=ell, hence r>=ell+1; bounding their count by the log of the repunit shows theta approaches 1/2 at the stated explicit rate. All primitives in an odd finite field are nonsquares, so half is a strict ceiling when NSNPs exist. Finite modular arithmetic is reproduced with integer code; no finite sampling stands in for the infinite steps.

originality.rationale: The same-object Zhou-Wu preprint establishes low-density sufficient bounds and character-sum conditions for short tuples but not explicit 13-runs at densities tending to 1/2. Cohen handles pair thresholds; an earlier result only handles adjacent pairs at a<=4 and one odd prime factor, neither of which implies this 13-run and limit. Searches of indexed mathematical findings and primary literature found no covering high-density theorem; explicit residual literature risks are recorded, and absence of a hit alone is not treated as novelty proof.

value.rationale: For the exact finite-field NSNP existence problem, the result determines the sharp but unattained upper primitive-density supremum simultaneously for all tuple lengths 3 through 13. It constructs infinitely many fields whose NSNP population has vanishing relative density while an explicit thirteen-term consecutive run persists, demonstrating that universal low-density threshold conditions cannot be interpreted as a clustering barrier. The natural thirteen-term run is certified over a fixed Fermat prime and persists at every odd extension degree, rather than an arbitrary isolated small-parameter computation.
